name: Wheat
soil: Well-drained loamy to clay-loam soil; optimal pH 6.5–7.5
seedRate: 100 kg/ha (timely sown), 125 kg/ha (late sown); row spacing 20–22.5 cm
fertilizerNPK: 120:60:40 kg N:P2O5:K2O per hectare + Zinc Sulphate 25 kg/ha if deficient
cultivationSteps: Land Preparation: 1 deep ploughing followed by 2–3 harrowings and planking for fine tilth (or Zero-Till seed drill after paddy).
Seed Treatment: Treat seeds with Carbendazim (2 g/kg) or Trichoderma (4 g/kg) against loose smut and termites.
Sowing: Sow with seed-cum-fertilizer drill at 4–5 cm depth between Nov 1–25 for optimal tillering.
Weed Control: Apply Sulfosulfuron or Clodinafop at 30–35 DAS for Phalaris minor (Gulli Danda).
Harvesting: Harvest when grain moisture drops to ~14% and straw turns golden yellow.

name: Rice (Paddy)
soil: Clayey to clay-loam alluvial soils with high water retention; optimal pH 5.5–6.8
seedRate: 20–25 kg/ha (transplanting) or 8–10 kg/ha (SRI method); spacing 20 × 15 cm
fertilizerNPK: 120:60:60 kg/ha (split N in 3 doses: basal, active tillering, panicle initiation)
cultivationSteps: Nursery Raising: Prepare raised wet nursery beds (1/10th area of main field) and transplant 21–25 day old seedlings.
Puddling & Levelling: Laser land levelling saves 20–25% water; puddle field to reduce percolation.
Transplanting / DSR: Transplant 2 seedlings/hill at 2–3 cm depth, or adopt Direct Seeded Rice (DSR) to cut labor & water.
Water Management: Maintain 2–5 cm standing water during vegetative & flowering stages; adopt Alternate Wetting & Drying (AWD).
Harvesting: Drain field 10 days before harvest; harvest when 80% panicles turn straw-colored.

name: Mustard (Rapeseed)
soil: Light to medium sandy loam; well-drained; optimal pH 6.5–7.8
seedRate: 4–5 kg/ha; row spacing 30–45 cm, plant-to-plant 10–15 cm (thinning at 15–20 DAS)
fertilizerNPK: 80:40:40 kg/ha + Sulphur 40 kg/ha (critical for oil content)
cultivationSteps: Field Prep: Fine, firm seedbed with conserved soil moisture.
Sowing: Sow Oct 1–25 at 2–3 cm depth; timely sowing minimizes aphid attack.
Thinning: Thin excess seedlings at 15–20 DAS to maintain 12 cm spacing for strong branching.
Sulphur Nutrition: Apply SSP or Gypsum/Bentonite Sulphur to boost oil content by 3–5%.
Harvesting: Harvest in early morning when 75% siliquae (pods) turn yellowish to prevent shattering.

name: Cotton
soil: Deep black cotton soil (Vertisols) or fertile alluvial soil; pH 6.5–8.0
seedRate: 2–2.5 kg/ha (Bt hybrids); spacing 90 × 60 cm or High-Density Planting (HDPS)
fertilizerNPK: 100:50:50 kg/ha + Magnesium Sulphate 2% foliar spray to prevent leaf reddening
cultivationSteps: Deep Summer Ploughing: Destroys Pink Bollworm pupae and soil-borne pathogens.
Sowing & Refuge: Sow on ridges/furrows; plant non-Bt refuge border rows to delay pest resistance.
IPM Monitoring: Install 5 pheromone traps/acre and yellow sticky traps from 45 DAS.
Drip Fertigation: Drip irrigation boosts cotton yield by 25–35% while saving 45% water.
Clean Picking: Pick dry, fully burst bolls in 3–4 rounds during morning hours.

name: Soybean
soil: Well-drained medium black or loamy soil; pH 6.0–7.2 (sensitive to waterlogging)
seedRate: 65–75 kg/ha; spacing 45 × 5 cm using Broad Bed Furrow (BBF) planter
fertilizerNPK: 30:60:40 kg/ha + 20 kg Sulphur (treat seed with Rhizobium japonicum + PSB)
cultivationSteps: BBF Planting: Broad Bed Furrow method drains excess monsoon rain and conserves moisture in dry spells.
Seed Inoculation: Treat with fungicide first, then Rhizobium + PSB biofertilizer right before sowing.
Weed Control: Keep weed-free for first 45 days via inter-cultivation or Imazethapyr at 15–20 DAS.
Pest Watch: Monitor for Girdle Beetle and Semi-looper caterpillars.
Harvesting: Harvest promptly when 95% pods turn brown and leaves drop.
irrigationSchedule: Mostly rainfed; protective irrigation at Flowering & Pod-filling if dry spell >15 days

name: Sugarcane
soil: Deep fertile loam to heavy alluvial soil; pH 6.5–7.5
seedRate: 35,000–40,000 three-bud setts/ha (or 12,000–15,000 single-bud seedlings under SSI)
cultivationSteps: Trench / Paired-Row Planting: Plant in 120 cm wide trenches to enable intercropping (potato/onion/moong) and drip irrigation.
Sett Treatment: Dip setts in Carbendazim (0.1%) + Imidacloprid before planting to stop Red Rot & termites.
Trash Mulching: Spread dry cane trash between rows to suppress weeds and conserve soil moisture.
Earthing Up & Propping: Perform heavy earthing up at 120 days and tie canes to prevent lodging.
Harvesting: Cut close to ground level when Brix reading reaches 18–20%.
irrigationSchedule: Every 7–10 days in summer, 15–20 days in winter; drip fertigation saves 50% water

name: Tomato
soil: Well-drained sandy loam rich in organic matter; pH 6.0–7.0
seedRate: 125–150 g/ha (hybrids) raised in cocopeat pro-trays under insect-proof net
fertilizerNPK: 120:80:80 kg/ha + Calcium Nitrate & Boron foliar spray to prevent Blossom End Rot
cultivationSteps: Healthy Nursery: Raise virus-free seedlings in 98-cell pro-trays under 40-mesh net for 25 days.
Raised Beds & Mulching: Use 30-micron silver-black plastic mulch + drip lines on raised beds.
Staking & Pruning: Provide bamboo/wire trellising for indeterminate hybrids to keep fruits clean.
IPM for Whitefly & Tuta: Install yellow sticky traps + pheromone traps; alternate neem oil & targeted sprays.
Harvesting: Pick at breaker/turning stage for long-distance mandi transport, red-ripe for local markets.
irrigationSchedule: Daily/alternate-day drip irrigation; avoid sudden moisture swings that cause fruit cracking

name: Potato
soil: Loose, friable sandy loam; optimal pH 5.5–6.5
seedRate: 25–30 quintals/ha of certified sprouted seed tubers (35–45 g size); spacing 60 × 20 cm
fertilizerNPK: 150:80:100 kg/ha (high Potash for tuber size and dry matter)
cultivationSteps: Pre-Sprouting: Keep seed tubers in diffused light 10–15 days prior for stout green sprouts.
Ridge Planting: Plant on 60 cm ridges at 5–7 cm depth; apply full P, K and 50% N as basal.
Earthing Up: Perform earthing up at 25–30 DAP along with top-dressing remaining 50% Urea to prevent tuber greening.
Late Blight Shield: Give preventive Mancozeb spray before foggy/cloudy spells.
Dehaulming & Curing: Cut haulms 10–12 days before digging so tuber skin hardens for cold storage.

name: Onion
soil: Deep friable loam rich in humus; well-drained; pH 6.0–7.0
seedRate: 6–8 kg/ha nursery seed; transplant 45-day seedlings at 15 × 10 cm spacing
fertilizerNPK: 100:50:50 kg/ha + 30–40 kg Sulphur (enhances pungency and storage life)
cultivationSteps: Raised Nursery: Raise seedlings on raised beds treated with Trichoderma to prevent damping-off.
Transplanting: Dip seedling roots in Carbendazim + Pseudomonas solution before transplanting.
Micro-Irrigation: Drip or micro-sprinklers yield uniform bulbs and reduce Purple Blotch disease.
Curing: Harvest when 50% tops fall over; windrow-cure in field shade for 4–5 days and trim necks at 2.5 cm.
Ventilated Storage: Store Rabi onions in well-ventilated Kanda Chawl structures for 4–6 months.
irrigationSchedule: Light frequent irrigation every 5–7 days; stop irrigation 12–15 days before harvest

name: Maize (Corn)
soil: Deep fertile well-drained loamy soil; pH 6.0–7.5
cultivationSteps: Ridge Sowing: Sow seeds on the side of ridges to avoid monsoon waterlogging.
Fall Armyworm Scouting: Inspect central whorl weekly from 15 DAS; apply Emamectin Benzoate or Spinetoram if needed.
Split Nitrogen: Top-dress Urea at knee-high (30 DAS) and tasseling (55 DAS) stages.
Harvesting: Harvest when cob husks dry and black layer forms at kernel base.

name: Chickpea (Chana / Gram)
soil: Well-drained loamy to black clay loam; pH 6.5–7.8
fertilizerNPK: 20:50:20 kg/ha (starter N + Rhizobium & PSB seed inoculation)
cultivationSteps: Wilt Prevention: Treat seed with Trichoderma viride (5 g/kg) + Carbendazim to prevent Fusarium Wilt.
Nipping: Nip top shoots at 35–40 DAS to encourage profuse lateral branching and higher pod count.
Pod Borer IPM: Install 5 pheromone traps/acre and bird perches (10/acre) for Helicoverpa armigera.
Harvesting: Harvest when leaves turn reddish-brown and pods rattle.
irrigationSchedule: Pod Development (75 DAS) — avoid excess water

name: Groundnut (Peanut)
soil: Loose sandy loam or red loam for easy peg penetration; pH 6.0–7.0
fertilizerNPK: 25:50:40 kg/ha + Gypsum 400 kg/ha at flowering (calcium is vital for pod filling)
cultivationSteps: Seed Treatment: Treat kernels with Tebuconazole (1.5 g/kg) + Rhizobium.
Gypsum Application: Band-apply Gypsum at 35–40 DAS near the pegging zone to prevent empty pods (pops).
Tikka Disease Watch: Spray Carbendazim + Mancozeb at 45–50 DAS if dark leaf spots appear.
Drying: Dry harvested pods down to <9% moisture to avoid Aflatoxin contamination.
